page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, running on an Intel Xeon processor with an x86_64 architecture and a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 13.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance is positioned at the lower tier of compute and memory capabilities. The single-core stress-ng score of 1105.58 and Geekbench single-core score of 944.0 fall into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is constrained by the dual-thread configuration, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1452.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1124.0, both placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 13.32 GB/sec for large block reads and 11.13 GB/sec for large block writes.

Given its hardware profile, the n1-highmem-2 is suited for workloads that require a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio but do not demand intensive computational power. Suitable applications include lightweight database operations, basic caching layers, and memory-bound utility scripts. However, intensive tasks such as large-scale software compilation, real-time ray tracing, and LLM inference are highly constrained, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 603.54 and a static web serving throughput of 1.58 GB/sec.
